title: Prefixed nominative (subject) pronoun forms
note: The subject proclitics that attach to the verb; the front of the agglutination chain (subject + TAM + root).

provenance.evidence: §54 'When prefixed to the verb the nominative case appears in the shortened forms: me- wo- ɔ- ɛ- ye- mo- wo- ...; together with the prefix a-: ma- woa- wa- yea- moa- woa-'. djvu flattened ɔ->o, ɛ->e, yɛ->ye, wɔ->wo.

dialect_note: Pan-Twi forms (identical in Asante + Akuapem); described by Christaller (Akuapem source) and corroborated against Asante wordforms (meko, oba, obeba, wonim, medi...). Fante neg-future kɔ- is the one variety-marked form.

title: Possessive pronoun forms
note: Distinct from the subject prefixes — 3sg is 'ne', NOT a verbal subject. Recorded to keep the verifier from treating possessives as subject prefixes.

provenance.evidence: §55 'In the possessive case: me my, wo thy, ne his/her/its, yɛn our, mo your, wɔn their'

dialect_note: Pan-Twi forms (identical in Asante + Akuapem); described by Christaller (Akuapem source) and corroborated against Asante wordforms (meko, oba, obeba, wonim, medi...). Fante neg-future kɔ- is the one variety-marked form.

title: Objective pronoun forms

provenance.evidence: §56 'In the objective case the prefix of ɔno, ɛno is dropped: me, wo, no, yɛn, mo, wɔn'; object 'no' often omitted for a thing

title: Verbal TAM prefixes
note: The aspect/tense markers that sit between the subject prefix and the verb root. Present = bare stem; preterit/continuative are marked by tone + palatal suffix (not a prefix).

forms.evidence: §91.1 'the Present tense ... the stem is in its bare form, i.e. without any prefix': ɔfa 'he takes'
'The Progressive form ... is formed by the prefix re-': ɔrefa 'he is taking'
'The first Future ... is formed by the prefix be-': ɔbɛfa 'he will take' (his 'be' = bɛ)
'The second Future ... is formed by the prefixes rebe-': ɔrebɛfa
'The Perfect tense ... is formed by the prefix a-'; fuses with subject (§54): ma-, wa-, yɛa-
§ 'F. in the negative future forms uses the prefix ko- instead of be-'

provenance.evidence: Prefix-formation statements (English prose, reliable in djvu) corroborated against leaf 90 §91 ten-forms overview. Prefixes re-/be-/rebe-/a- are ASCII-clean; only bɛ carries the ɛ.

dialect_note: Pan-Twi forms (identical in Asante + Akuapem); described by Christaller (Akuapem source) and corroborated against Asante wordforms (meko, oba, obeba, wonim, medi...). Fante neg-future kɔ- is the one variety-marked form.

title: Verbal agglutination order
rule: A finite verb word = SUBJECT-prefix + (TAM-prefix) + ROOT (+ object/suffix). Example: yɛ+bɛ+ma -> yɛbɛma 'we will give'; ɔ+re+fa -> ɔrefa 'he is taking'; me+a+ba -> maba 'I have come'.
note: This order is what morphophon.decompose() strips in reverse to verify agglutinated forms against known roots.

provenance.evidence: §54 prefixed nominative forms + the perfect-a fusion table establish subject+TAM+root ordering
